title: variety@1: a regional variety or historical stage
description: languages/<language>/varieties/<id>/meta.json. Gives only what differs from its parent; every field it leaves out (nativeName, scripts, characterKeys, speech and so on) is inherited. Content files next to it hold only entries that differ from the parent's.

id.description: Unique across every language and variety. Must match the folder name.

parent.description: The id of the language or variety this one sits under: the language whose varieties/ folder holds it, or another variety of that language.

kind.description: standard: another standard norm of the language (for example a national norm). regional: a dialect or related regional language. historical: an earlier stage.

nativeName.description: The name in the language itself.

code.description: ISO 639-3 code (three lowercase letters) or Glottolog code (four letters and four digits).

period.description: When a historical stage was spoken or written. Years are integers, negative for BCE. Required for historical.

reconstructed.description: True for a stage known only by reconstruction (for example Old Chinese). Its sources name the reconstruction it follows.

scripts.description: Writing systems, in the order the learner shows them.

characterKeys.description: Character Learner script keys. Empty when the language has no Character Learner script.

romanization.description: Romanization systems used, main one first (for example jyutping, pinyin, hepburn).

speech.description: BCP 47 tag for text to speech.

font.description: A special font the language needs, such as pIqaD.
